answer.rationale: Current situation: p99 latency 5x target, release 2h old, settlement peak with heavy writes. Memory_b1 shows rollback is fast and safe for checkout errors. Memory_b2 is critical—it warns that regional failover during hot writes caused a 40-minute replication gap and lost writes for two accounts. This directly applies: settlement traffic means writes are absolutely hot right now, so failover is contraindicated. Rollback of the suspect release is the only action that (1) addresses root cause rather than symptoms, (2) avoids the write-loss risk of failover, (3) works on the timeline we have. Memory_b3 suggests capacity headroom exists, but add_capacity takes time we don't have at peak. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) are good for dependency faults, not release regressions. Read replicas (memory_b5) help dashboard load, not write-path latency. A rollback starts immediately, clears the suspect build, and memory_b1 proves it worked before without customer impact. We verify b1 and b2 to confirm: rollback is proven safe, and failover is proven dangerous under current conditions. Small guarded test scale allows us to monitor the rollback on a subset before full commitment if needed.
